headline: Curated references and portable tools sharpen microbial profiling and genome workflows
label: Microbial Profiling And Genome Tooling
summary: An updated mOTUs-db, species-level 16S resources, and browser-native and Nextflow tooling target interoperable microbial and comparative genomics analysis.
synthesis: The dominant thread is improving microbial taxonomic profiling through curated reference data and interoperable tooling. The mOTUs-db update links taxonomy to genome-encoded function and environmental and geographic distributions, with a CLI and API for profiling. RADSuite pairs RADlib, a curated 16S rRNA gene copy database, with RADx, which identifies sequenced variable regions, to support species-level identification. VPHYL, an R Shiny app, converts Emu and EPI2ME wf-16s nanopore 16S abundance tables into phyloseq or BIOM objects with automated HTML reports. Sparrowhawk adds a deployment angle: a WebAssembly framework for browser-based tools that run locally, keeping data private, demonstrated with lightweight microbial genomics methods. On the genome side, nf-core/pairgenomealign wraps LAST pairwise whole-genome alignment in a scalable Nextflow pipeline with benchmarking, and ABAQS scores annotation quality via completeness, gene model validity and protein profile accuracy across over 1700 fungal genomes. Scopes differ; no cross-tool performance comparisons are supported.
